text:
**For most buyers, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** All six guides in the search results point the same way.

**Why LiFePO4 usually wins**
- **Cycle life:** LiFePO4 stations are typically rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500 to 1,000 for NMC (one guide says up to 2,000). At one full cycle a day, that's about 8 years versus under 2 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Safety:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly, with lower peak temperatures and less gas. One test found smoke without flames, while all the NMC cells ignited. LFP isn't fireproof, though. In one overcharge test it reached runaway earlier, so a quality battery management system still matters. It's a real advantage for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Price:** The premium has mostly disappeared. One retailer's data shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LiFePO4 versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Most new mid-size and large models are LiFePO4.

**Where NMC still has an edge**
- NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the inverter, case, and ports weigh the same either way. One database found only about 10% difference at the median, and some LFP units are lighter per Wh than NMC ones ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Compare actual specs rather than assuming.
- If you'll use it only a few times a year, NMC's lower cycle count may never matter. Calendar aging will limit it first.

**Cold weather isn't a clear differentiator.** Most stations of either type, LFP or NMC, won't charge below 32°F. Check the specific model's manual ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). One guide claims NMC is much worse in the cold, but the others say the limits depend more on the maker than on the chemistry.

**Bottom line**
- **Daily or frequent use** (van, cabin, solar, UPS): LiFePO4.
- **Home outage backup:** LiFePO4. It lasts longer and fails more gently.
- **Weight-critical and rarely used:** compare specific models, since either chemistry can work.
- Don't replace a working NMC unit just for the chemistry.

**A LiFePO4 example for home backup:** the [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) has 2,073.6 Wh, a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating to 80%, and a 5-year warranty. It lists at $899, and the page says code AFF5OFF takes $44.95 off, bringing it to $854.05. It isn't expandable, and at 24.2 kg it isn't a carry-anywhere unit. Prices and codes change, so check at checkout.

The guides also name other LiFePO4 stations, the Anker SOLIX C1000 and EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus. The search results didn't include buy links for them, so I haven't linked any.

Whichever chemistry you pick, check the cycle rating's end point (80% versus 70%) and size the unit to what you need to run first.
